feedback: The confession follows the exact contradiction I used: his own query quotes the original-contents condition, so denying prior knowledge was untenable. Taking poison at the preview and using the later private glass describes actions inferred from previously available access, rather than unveiling a new route or hidden object. The motive also follows his fear of public scholarly humiliation. His lines to Reed and Dada give the ending some emotional consequence beyond admitting mechanics. Elle and Monet admitting their financial lies makes the competing explanations coherent; they do not suddenly acquire alibis. The outcome feels earned, although the final certainty necessarily comes from confession because the physical opportunities were shared.
